HTML specimens are reference-only visual artifacts under do-not-port-specimen-markup; the build proves real loading/empty/error states and responsive 375px to 1440px with a bootable React+TypeScript prototype

alternatives: Allow live model calls behind a flag
Allow minimal backend proxy for fixtures
decisions.choice: All model traffic is stubbed and deterministic in the frontend; no network model calls, no backend orchestration, no billing hooks in this Run.
rationale: Base prompt and Run contract require stubbed sessions and tool trace with frontend only; real traffic would violate non-goals and the evaluation repeatability.
Deterministic fixtures let later phases prove loading/empty/error states without flakiness.
risks: Stub realism gap: later Roles may over-fit to fixtures and under-design streaming, latency, and failure nuance.
revisitWhen: A future Run explicitly charters live model integration.

alternatives: Single global right panel shared across sessions
Right panel as modal overlay only
decisions.choice: Left sidebar is global (projects > sessions); right sidebar is per-session scoped (browser, files, GitHub tabs follow the active session); center column owns conversation plus customizable input bar with follow-ups and mode toggles.
rationale: Base prompt names left project/session sidebar and right per-session sidebar with the three views; scoping the right panel per session preserves context when switching sessions.
Fixing the contract now prevents Directions from collapsing the workbench into a single-column chatbot.
risks: Three-pane density is hard at 375px; responsive strategy must collapse sidebars into drawers without losing scope semantics.
revisitWhen: Usability evidence shows session-switching confusion attributable to scoping.

alternatives: Hide tool calls behind a debug toggle
decisions.choice: Agent tool calls (Write, Read, Edit, Bash, WebSearch) are first-class visible trace attached to assistant turns, with summary-first progressive disclosure to full detail; stub fixtures cover running, succeeded, failed, and empty states.
rationale: Base prompt explicitly requires visible tool calls; transparency is the differentiator over generic chatbots and the basis of user trust.
Summary-first disclosure keeps the reading instrument calm while preserving auditability.
risks: Over-verbose traces could overwhelm the central column; information-tier discipline is required in surface architecture.
revisitWhen: Streaming/error-state evidence demands a revised trace model.

risks: Stub realism gap: deterministic fixtures may under-represent streaming latency, partial failures, and long traces, leading Directions to under-design those states.
Three-pane density versus 375px single column: collapsing two sidebars into drawers without losing per-session scope semantics is the highest interaction risk.
Mode taxonomy is invented downstream: inconsistent mode semantics across Directions could confuse steering; surface architecture must bound it.
Mock GitHub/browser views may read as live integrations; clear static-mock framing is needed to avoid false affordances.
summary: Grounded the agentic model chat Surface: builder user directing and verifying stubbed agent work via three-pane workbench (left sessions, central composer with follow-ups/modes, per-session browser/files/GitHub panel, visible Write/Read/Edit/Bash/WebSearch trace). Product Brief and Constraint Draft produced with cited hard floors, operational perception terms, data contracts, and open creative space; no blockers; requesting advance.
